content.text: Instagram登录注册帖子标记内容轮播Good morning! Severe thunderstorms capable of tornadoes, damaging winds, and very large hail are expected to develop this afternoon across the state. The best chance for tornadoes will occur from 4-7pm when storms are maturing but also somewhat discrete. Please have multiple ways to receive weather alerts this afternoon and evening! Lots of good information in the three attached images, so be sure to look them over! I will likely be unable to provide additional updates today, but will try to sneak something in if any significant changes to the forecast occur.*SEVERE STORMS WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR TORNADOES ON MONDAY* Severe storms will be possible across much of Wisconsin Monday afternoon and evening with the potential for tornadoes, large hail, and damaging winds. The Storm Prediction Center has issued a rare moderate (level 4/5) risk of severe storms for west-central WI, and an enhanced (level 3/5) risk of severe storms elsewhere across the state. With that said, rather significant confidence issues exist regarding the overall risk. Head over the Meteorologist Nicholas Kniprath on Facebook for a more detailed look post! #wiwx #wisconsin #wisconsinweatherA winter storm continues to impact the state with moderate to heavy snow and gusty winds, with BLIZZARD CONDITIONS expected across East-Central Wisconsin. TIMING: Moderate to heavy snowfall will continue for east-central and far northeast Wisconsin this evening into the overnight, with light to moderate snowfall occurring for much of the remainder of the state. By daybreak Saturday, light snow will be ongoing across the state. Expect light snows to taper off through the afternoon hours Saturday. Winds will be strongest this evening into the overnight before easing through the day Saturday. ALERTS: The latest weather alerts can be found at www.weather.gov FORECAST DISCUSSION: A short forecast and discussion this evening… The snowfall forecast from this morning has appeared to play out well so far southeast of a Eau Claire to Rhinelander line given widespread reports of 6-12”. The forecast might even end up being a little low in the 8-14” area from this morning, as reports + additional forecast amounts suggest isolated amounts up to 16-18” could occur when the storm is all said and done. North of that Eau Claire to Rhinelander line, the forecast was not nearly as close. The dry air won the battle today, leading to overall amounts 2-5” lower than originally forecast in the area. Nonetheless, I’ll do a full storm/forecast recap when this system is fully over. Now, a few quick notes about the additional snow forecast: Firstly, this is additional snow after 6pm this evening, so subtract what has fallen since then to get the true additional forecast for your location. Secondly, Confidence is quite high in these additional amounts, but it could still be a little high if things go wrong. What could go wrong? 1-The winds blowing apart the snow crystals leading to less amounts, 2-Dry air continuing to win in far western areas, and 3-A more rapid end to the snowfall Saturday morning. But even given these concerns, the ranges listed *should* capture that potential well.Good morning! Here's an updated snowfall forecast map based on the latest data and the current weather alerts. UPDATED FORECAST DISCUSSION: Slight adjustments to snowfall totals were made across the area. Main change was to bring the 8-14" area further north into central Wisconsin given the latest guidance. TIMING: Moderate to heavy snow is expected to overspread much of the state this morning (far northwestern areas may remain mostly dry). Wind gusts will also slowly increase across the area this morning. This afternoon, a lull in the snow is possible, but not certain, and winds will continue to increase. This evening through daybreak Saturday, moderate to heavy snow is expected across the state, with near whiteout conditions likely at times. During the day Saturday, winds will remain gusty and the snow showers may be slow to exit the state. IMPACTS: Travel is expected to be difficult to impossible this afternoon through Saturday morning. The worst travel conditions are expected this evening through mid-morning Saturday. Continued light snow and gusty winds through the day Saturday will make conditions slow to improve. CONFIDENCE: Confidence in the timing of this storm is high. Confidence in gusty winds leading to near whiteout conditions at times is high. Confidence in forecast snowfall amounts is medium-high. ALERTS: A slew of weather alerts are in effect across the state. Visit www.weather.gov and click on your city on the map for the latest alert information.轮播A significant winter storm is expected to impact the region Friday and Saturday, bringing widespread heavy snowfall amounts and gusty winds, leading to likely treacherous travel conditions for many across the state. If you have travel plans Friday or Saturday across the Upper Midwest, now is the time to consider delaying/canceling those plans. TIMING: Moderate to heavy snow is expected to overspread much of the state from late tonight through mid morning Friday (far northwestern areas may remain mostly dry). Friday morning, wind gusts will also slowly increase across the area. Friday afternoon, a lull in the snow is possible, but not certain, and winds will continue to increase. Friday evening through daybreak Saturday, moderate to heavy snow is expected across the state, with near whiteout conditions likely at times. During the day Saturday, winds will remain gusty and the snow showers may be slow to exit the state. IMPACTS: Travel is expected to be difficult to impossible Friday through Saturday morning. The worst travel conditions are expected Friday evening through mid-morning Saturday. Continued light snow and gusty winds through the day Saturday will make conditions slow to improve. CONFIDENCE: Confidence in the timing of this storm is high. Confidence in gusty winds leading to near whiteout conditions at times is high. Confidence in forecast snowfall amounts is medium. ALERTS: A slew of weather alerts are in effect across the state. Visit www.weather.gov and click on your city on the map for the latest alert information. FORECAST DISCUSSION: To see the technical forecast discussion, visit the Meteorologist Nicholas Kniprath page on Facebook.A significant winter storm is expected to impact the Upper Midwest Friday, with major travel disruptions likely as a result of heavy snow and gusty winds. Areas most likely to see heavy snow are south of a La Crosse to Wausaukee line, but shifts in the forecast remain possible. TIMING: Snow begins to overspread the area after midnight Thursday night and should overspread most of the state (except northwest areas) by daybreak Friday. The heaviest snows are expected during the daylight hours Friday. Snow tapers off from west to east late Friday night, with only lingering snow showers for Saturday. However, winds will remain quite breezy Saturday, leading to some continued blowing/drifting of the snow. IMPACTS: Travel conditions are expected to be difficult to near impossible at times Friday across central and southern Wisconsin given heavy snowfall rates and gusty winds. Travel conditions will likely be slow to improve on Saturday as breezy conditions linger. CONFIDENCE: Confidence is very high that a winter storm will impact central/southern Wisconsin on Friday leading to dangerous travel conditions. Confidence in the exact snowfall amounts is medium-low. Confidence levels should increase through the day Thursday and more high-res guidance becomes available. ALERTS: Winter storm watches have been issued by the NWS for areas most likely to experience major travel disruptions from this winter storm. FORECAST DISCUSSION: To see the technical forecast discussion, visit the Meteorologist Nicholas Kniprath Facebook page.A potent storm system begins to track into the region tonight, with multiple precipitation types expected for many over the next couple days. TIMING: Areas north of HWY 29 will be looking at mixed precipitation (rain/snow mix or quite possibly freezing rain) late tonight into early Wednesday morning. Areas south of HWY 8 will transition to rain for the daytime hours Wednesday. A more rapid transition (from NW to SE) from rain to snow will take place Wednesday after sunset. Expect most areas to see at least some snowfall accumulation (probably wet/slushy snow) late Wednesday night into later Thursday morning. IMPACTS: The greatest travel impacts on Wednesday will be north of highway 29 due to freezing rain (especially north of HWY 8). More widespread travel impacts are possible Wednesday night into Thursday. #wiwx #wisconsin #wisconsinweather #snow #freezingrainSevere thunderstorms are possible this evening across central and southern Wisconsin, where a slight (level 2 out of 5) risk of severe weather has been issued by the Storm Prediction Center. The main risk currently appears to be damaging winds, but a few instances of large hail and a brief spin up tornado or two will be possible. Additionally, these storms will be producing very heavy rainfall on a mostly frozen ground, likely leading to widespread ponding of water. #wiwxAn ice storms is expected to impact portions of Wisconsin late tonight into Saturday. Travel will be extremely dangerous to impossible at times across portions of northern and central Wisconsin early Saturday morning through Sunday morning. If you have travel plans generally along and north of HWY 29 Saturday, now is the time to cancel or delay them. #wiwxA winter storm is still expected to impact all of Wisconsin on Tuesday, with freezing rain south, a mix central, and all snow north. Travel will be treacherous and dangerous at times on Tuesday. Consider cancelling all unnecessary travel plans for the day Tuesday. #wiwx #wisconsin #weatherHere is your updated storm total snowfall and ice forecast (this does include the snow that has already fallen across far northwestern Wisconsin). However, the majority of this precipitation is expected late Monday evening through Tuesday evening. #wiwx #weather #wisconsinA winter storm is expected to bring *multiple rounds* of precipitation to Wisconsin beginning Monday morning and lasting into late Tuesday night.
